$description: Chromasmith design-token source of truth (W3C DTCG format). Seeded from chromasmith-design/project/_ds/.../_ds_manifest.json plus every variable declared in chromasmith-22.html's :root (~50-98), its body.light override (~1263-1301), and the token block in desktop/library-ui.js (~695-776). Matched by computed value AND property role per docs/ui-workflow/STATE.md S1(a) (fontSize->--fs-*, spacing/gap->--sp-*, radius->--r*) — never by _ds var() name (fewer than 10% of wireframe declarations use one). Every app variable is either a token below ($extensions.chromasmith.appVar) or listed in design/token-conflicts.md. Generated by /tmp .../build_tokens.py — do not hand-edit without regenerating from source; see design/verify_tokens.py.

root.commentBefore:
/* Wireframe accent swap: amber -> Mist Blue (dark)/Blue Slate (light), the Design System's own
     --primary-on-dark/--primary pair (desktop/library-ui.js's DS token block). Verified >=4.5:1
     against every background it sits on as text/icon colour (measured, not eyeballed — see
     body.light's own --acc override below for the light-theme numbers). */
  /* --acc2 was an invented off-palette blue (#4a9ddc/#1f68a0) — the DS is explicit that there is
     no second brand accent (design.md: "There is no second brand accent"), so it now aliases
     --acc directly rather than diverging. --ok/--err below are the DS's own --green-pine/
     --red-oxide UNCHANGED for light mode; dark mode keeps its brighter values on purpose — DS's
     literals are near-invisible on this near-black --bg (contrast ~1.3:1), so darkroom
     readability wins there (see body.light's override for the light-mode DS values). */

bodyLight.commentBefore:
/* Re-measured 2026-09-09 for the wireframe's Blue Slate (#224455), replacing the darkened-amber
     value this comment used to document. Blue Slate against white/--sur2(#f5f5f7)/the old
     #f4f3ef reference is 10.4:1 / 9.5:1 / 9.3:1 — clears 4.5:1 with enormous margin (it's the
     DS's own dark, saturated brand navy, not a hue needing correction the way amber did), so no
     further darkening was needed. --acc2 now aliases --acc (DS: "no second brand accent" —
     see :root's comment). --ok/--err switched from their previously-measured darkened values to
     the DS's own --green-pine/--red-oxide literals unchanged: against white they're 10:1+/8:1+,
     clearing 4.5:1 with the same enormous margin as Blue Slate, so no re-darkening was needed
     here either (dark mode keeps its brighter values — DS's literals go near-invisible on
     near-black, see :root's comment); the existing rgba(212,144,58,…) chip/badge TINTS are
     untouched literals, so a chip's translucent background stays the familiar warm amber while
     the text sitting on it stays legible — the same "container / on-container" pairing Material
     Design uses for exactly this problem, arrived at independently by measuring rather than by
     copying it.
     Only text/icon color changes; --acc still paints .bpri's button gradient and .fx-toggle.on's
     track, both of which read FINE darker (only helps their contrast against black/white). */

chromasmith.decision: resolved 2026-09-11: adopt DS (no second accent) — aliased to --acc in both modes

root.commentBefore:
/* ── TYPE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
     ⚠️ --mono is for NUMERALS, code and the build stamp. It is not a UI voice. It used to be:
     81 uses against 8 of --sans, with 23 `text-transform:uppercase` rules on top, which made
     almost every label uppercase letter-spaced monospace — the tell that reads as generated
     "technical" UI rather than a photo tool. Mainstream photo/grading apps (LR, C1, DRK, Dehancer)
     all set labels in a neutral grotesque and reserve monospace for numbers. Uppercase now survives
     in exactly ONE role (the panel/section eyebrow) so it still reads as a system.
     --serif is kept as an alias of --display purely so older rules keep resolving. */

root.commentBefore:
/* Elevation tokens — a top-light inset (mimics a physical panel catching ambient light from
     above, the same trick macOS's own translucent materials use) plus a soft drop shadow, so
     surfaces read as raised trays rather than flat rectangles drawn with a 1px outline. Kept as
     tokens (not hand-repeated box-shadow lists) so every card/control panel/menu stays visually
     consistent and any future tuning is a one-line change. */

bodyLight.commentBefore:
/* No white inset — on a light card it either vanishes (near-white on white) or, at any opacity
     high enough to show, reads as a stray pale rim rather than a highlight. A plain, much softer
     shadow is the whole treatment; light surfaces read as "raised" from the shadow alone. Alpha
     is roughly a third of the dark values (.06/.10 vs .3/.35) because the same shadow strength
     that disappears into a near-black background is heavy and muddy on near-white. */

lift1.$description: No DS token matches this multi-layer recipe (DS --shadow-product is single-layer, imagery-only per DS guideline) — see conflicts.

lift2.$description: No DS token match — see conflicts.

bodyLight.commentBefore:
/* The slider thumb's #e9e6df was a hardcoded literal, not a token — cream-on-white, close to
